domains.name: Element 1: Basic radio law and operating practice

domain_guidance.summary: Covers basic radio law and operating practice with which every maritime radio operator should be completely familiar, including rules, regulations, international treaties, and operational procedures for commercial services.

Focuses on general radiotelephone electronic fundamentals and advanced techniques needed to properly adjust, repair, troubleshoot, and maintain complex radio transmitters and receivers in commercial operations across various regulated services.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Bring required official identification and any necessary documentation to your test center. Ensure you fully understand the question format across Element 1 and Element 3 before starting your session.

faq.answer_text: The examination consists of a total of 124 questions distributed across the designated written examination elements required by the Federal Communications Commission for commercial operators.
faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?

faq.answer_text: The passing score for the certification requires achieving 18 out of 24 on Element 1 and successfully scoring 75 out of 100 on Element 3.
You should check directly with the Federal Communications Commission or your designated test administrator for specific timing and duration details regarding your scheduled examination session.
Yes, this certification examination is completely current and active. Please check with the Federal Communications Commission for the most up to date certification path details.

editorial.meta_description: Prepare for the FCC GROL General Radiotelephone Operator License covering 124 total questions, basic radio law, and electronic fundamentals for commercial.

methodology.summary: This page was built using official Federal Communications Commission exam guides and regulatory documents to present factual requirements for the commercial operator license.

editorial.overview: The FCC GROL General Radiotelephone Operator License is certified by the Federal Communications Commission. It validates knowledge and skills required for commercial radio operators, covering basic radio law, operating practices, and electronic fundamentals necessary to properly adjust, repair, and maintain radio transmitters and receivers across various regulated telecommunications services with a total of 124 questions.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Carefully review current Federal Communications Commission question pools and official documentation for Element 1 and Element 3. Study electronic fundamentals, radio laws, treaties, regulations, and operating practices for maritime and aviation services extensively before scheduling your test to achieve the passing score of 18 out of 24 on Element 1.
editorial.who_should_take: Radio operators, professional technicians, and engineering personnel working in aviation and maritime radio services who need to service, maintain, or operate regulated radio transmitting equipment.
